records.title: Audit hash chain can fork under concurrent same-scope writes
records.baseline_evidence: backend/app/audit.py:35-39 (prev_hash read without lock) and audit.py:69-95 (verification walks seq order)
records.impact: Two concurrent audit writes in one event_scope (e.g. the default 'global' scope used by auth/login from two API processes) read the same prev_hash and fork the chain; audit_verify then reports false breaks, destroying the tamper-evidence value under normal traffic.
records.proposed_fix: Serialize chain-head updates per scope: lock a chain_heads row FOR UPDATE (or pg_advisory_xact_lock on scope) inside the writing transaction, then read head, insert, update head; add a concurrent-write test.

records.proposed_fix: Implement a periodic checkpoint export job signing chain head+seq with a key held outside the DB into separate storage, an unanchored-interval alert, and a scheduled chain_verify job; correct the docstring until then.

records.title: Concurrent same-key submissions return 500 instead of the stored receipt
records.baseline_evidence: backend/app/routers/submissions.py:123-139 (SELECT-then-INSERT, no ON CONFLICT handling); migrations/0001_init.sql:391 (unique (author_id, idempotency_key)); tests/test_idempotency.py:26-36 (sequential retries only)
records.impact: API-04a/G2-01 (S1) require concurrent same-key requests to converge to one receipt; a racing retry hits the unique index and gets an unhandled IntegrityError (500 INTERNAL_ERROR) instead of the receipt. No duplicate is created, but the convergence guarantee and the gate's 'five concurrent' test cannot pass.
records.proposed_fix: Handle the unique violation (or insert ... ON CONFLICT) and re-read the stored row, returning the receipt or 409 on hash mismatch exactly like the pre-check; add a concurrent same-key test.

records.title: No per-participant sealed bundles or T0 key release
records.baseline_evidence: grep AES/GCM/nonce/seal in backend/app: only status-word 'seal' in admin.py:299-300,670; errors.py:37 defines KEY_NOT_AVAILABLE (425) but no route raises it

records.title: Concurrent same-key idempotency requests race to an unhandled 500

records.proposed_fix: Weight location_score by span (e.g. 1.0 only when report span <= planted span+tolerance, linear decay beyond; or scale by planted_span/report_span), raise the alias threshold for wide spans, and route max-span overlapping reports to needs_review instead of auto-accept.

records.title: Rate limiter is in-process only, resets on restart, and never evicts keys

records.title: No scheduler leader lock; auto-submit scan runs unguarded on every worker

records.title: Auto-accept is live without the 99% precision validation gate

records.title: No cross-tab refresh coordination (Web Locks / BroadcastChannel)

records.proposed_fix: Wrap performRefresh in navigator.locks.request with a BroadcastChannel fallback so one tab refreshes and broadcasts the result.

records.title: Session-expired UX (P-23) and 'signed in on another device' variant missing

records.title: Draft sync: 3s fixed interval, no pagehide/sendBeacon flush, conflict auto-discards local edits, no status chips

records.title: Idempotency key discarded on failed attempt, breaking the stability guarantee
records.baseline_evidence: frontend/src/pages/participant/Workspace.tsx:404-419 and 445-451 (catch resets idemKey.current on any ApiRequestError, including network failures from api.ts:131-138); new key per attempt via newIdempotencyKey() api.ts:178-181
records.impact: If a POST reached the server but the response was lost, the participant's next click re-submits with a fresh key: duplicate report, burning per-file/per-round caps and risking penalties.
records.proposed_fix: Keep the key stable across retries of the same logical submission; regenerate only after a definitive server rejection or user reset; pair with outbox retry.

records.title: DELETE /me/sessions/{id} revokes another user's refresh tokens (IDOR)
records.baseline_evidence: backend/app/routers/auth.py:639-652: app.sessions UPDATE is scoped by user_id, but UPDATE app.refresh_tokens SET status='revoked' WHERE session_id = CAST(:sid AS uuid) (lines 648-651) has no user scoping; session ids are time-ordered UUIDv7 (backend/app/db.py:81-88)
records.impact: Any authenticated participant who obtains or guesses another user's session UUID (UUIDv7 embeds a timestamp) can revoke that user's refresh-token family, force-logging them out (targeted DoS on participants and staff)
records.proposed_fix: Scope the refresh_tokens update to the caller's sessions (WHERE session_id IN (SELECT id FROM app.sessions WHERE id = :sid AND user_id = :u)), return 404 when no own session matched, keep both updates in one transaction

records.title: Default JWT secret and dev DB credentials ship in code with no production fail-fast
records.baseline_evidence: backend/app/config.py:24-26 (app_api:app_api_dev / gt_admin:gt_admin_dev DSNs) and config.py:32 (jwt_secret default "dev-only-insecure-secret-replace-me"); the same secret derives the Fernet successor key (security.py:29), receipt HMAC (security.py:121), flag HMAC (security.py:127) and IP hashes (security.py:132); no startup guard validates overrides
records.impact: A deployment that sets ENVIRONMENT=production but forgets JWT_SECRET (or the DSNs) boots silently with a publicly known secret: universal token forgery (any role), refresh-successor decryption, forgeable receipts/flag codes and IP hashes
records.proposed_fix: Fail fast at startup when environment=production: refuse to boot if jwt_secret equals the dev default or is weak, and require non-default DSNs; warn loudly otherwise; derive the Fernet key from a separate setting to limit blast radius

records.title: Password-reset tokens are printed to stdout/logs

records.impact: Anyone with access to process logs (shared terminals, log aggregation, docker logs, cloud consoles) can read a live single-use 30-minute reset token and take over any account including admin
records.proposed_fix: Never print raw reset tokens; store them hashed like invites and surface them only via a step-up-gated organizer console endpoint or a real email provider; add secret-leak lint rules for print/log statements

records.title: In-process rate limiter: per-worker limits, restart resets, unbounded key growth

records.impact: Brute-force protection is only as strong as one worker (multiple uvicorn workers keep separate buckets; restart clears them); an unauthenticated attacker can grow _bucket without bound by sending unique emails to /auth/login (permanent dict entry with up to 60 floats each) - slow memory-exhaustion DoS and weakened per-account throttling
records.proposed_fix: Move the limiter to a shared store (Postgres/Redis) or bound the dict with TTL/LRU eviction and cap distinct keys per IP; DB-backed authoritative caps already exist for submissions - port that pattern to login/reset/step-up

records.title: No Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options headers
records.baseline_evidence: backend/app/main.py:87-89 sets only X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control; no CSP or frame-ancestors anywhere in backend or frontend (frontend/index.html:1-18, frontend/vite.config.ts)
records.impact: Defense-in-depth gap: a future injection point or compromised dependency would run without a CSP backstop; the console can be framed (clickjacking). Limited today because React escapes all rendering, tokens live in memory and the refresh cookie is SameSite=Strict/path-scoped
records.proposed_fix: Add a strict CSP (default-src 'self', no inline scripts, frame-ancestors 'none' / X-Frame-Options: DENY) at the reverse proxy or the FastAPI middleware for SPA and API responses

records.title: Upload/body size checks trust Content-Length and read-before-check
records.baseline_evidence: backend/app/main.py:69-84 rejects oversize bodies only when a parsable content-length header exceeds the cap (chunked encoding bypasses); admin file upload reads the whole part into memory before checking size: admin.py:572-574 (content = await file.read(); then if len(content) > 512*1024). Participant artifact path is correct (levels.py:803-807 bounded read)
records.impact: A step-up-authorized organizer can exhaust API memory with a huge chunked multipart part (pre-authenticated DoS); any client can bypass the generic body-size middleware using chunked transfer encoding
records.proposed_fix: Stream uploads with a bounded reader (read(max+1) chunks) and enforce a hard request-body cap independent of headers (ASGI middleware counting streamed bytes)

records.title: Negative limit query params bypass result caps
records.baseline_evidence: backend/app/routers/announcements.py:15-24 (min(limit, 100), no lower bound; negative LIMIT in PostgreSQL means no limit) and backend/app/routers/admin.py:1051-1074 (/admin/audit min(limit, 500))
records.impact: /v1/announcements?limit=-1 and /v1/admin/audit?limit=-1 return every row - unbounded result sets, cheap resource-exhaustion probe, inconsistent pagination
records.proposed_fix: Use FastAPI Query(ge=1, le=100) / le=500) constraints instead of min()
